mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances when the federal funds rate increases by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3 percentage points in a month signals an improving labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business confidence increase.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances when the unemployment rate drops by more than 0.3 percentage points in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three months signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances when RSAFS increases over three months.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month signals increased economic activity, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 70% of the instances when INDPRO increases by more than 1% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a tight labor market with strong job growth, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment increase.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and PAYEMS increases > 200,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances when UNRATE is below 4% and PAYEMS increases by more than 200,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 5% in a month and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) remains stable (less than 0.2% increase), it signals strong demand without significant inflationary pressure, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer confidence and spending remain robust.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 5% and CPIAUCSL increases < 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 50% of the instances when HOUST increases by more than 5% and CPIAUCSL increases by less than 0.2% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% in a month signals a shift towards accommodative monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as financial conditions ease.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are negative in more than 70% of the instances when the federal funds rate decreases by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) decreases by more than 1% in a month and GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative over the previous quarter, it signals a contraction in economic activity, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings and economic outlook worsen.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases > 1% in 1 month and GDPC1 < 0% in 3 months
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of the S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances when INDPRO decreases by more than 1% in a month and GDPC1 growth is negative over the previous quarter.
